title: HE TAUGHT YOU TO BE STRONG… BUT NEVER TOLD YOU WHERE TO PUT THE PAIN
paragraphs:
HE TAUGHT YOU TO BE STRONG… BUT NEVER TOLD YOU WHERE TO PUT THE PAIN
Why Men Hide Their Pain—and the Quiet War Destroying Them from the Inside
Somewhere between “be a man” and “don’t cry,” something sacred got buried.
Not killed. Not healed. Buried.
And buried things don’t disappear… they rot in silence.

He laughs louder than everyone else in the room, but no one notices how quickly he goes quiet when the conversation turns real. He provides, protects, performs—yet feels like he’s slowly disappearing in his own life. He says “I’m fine” with a smile that doesn’t reach his eyes, and the world accepts it because that’s what men are supposed to say.
Strong. Silent. Stable.
But no one ever taught him what to do with the ache.
The Scriptures never told men to become emotional vaults. That was culture. That was pride. That was survival.

Because when God formed man in the beginning, He didn’t design him to carry pain alone. In Genesis 2:7, the Hebrew says: “וַיִּיצֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָאָדָם” (Vayyitser YHWH Elohim et-ha’adam) — “Then the LORD God formed the man.” The word “וַיִּיצֶר” (vayyitser) is deeply intimate—it carries the sense of careful, intentional forming, like a potter shaping something fragile with both hands.
You were never built to be numb. You were shaped with intention… including your emotions.
But somewhere along the way, men learned that feeling deeply was dangerous.
So they buried it.

They buried the rejection from their father who never said “I’m proud of you.”
They buried the heartbreak from the woman who walked away.
They buried the fear of failure, the shame of addiction, the weight of expectations.
And what happens to buried pain?
It doesn’t stay buried.

It leaks out in anger.
It leaks out in distance.
It leaks out in addictions no one talks about.
It leaks out in silence that slowly kills relationships.
Even David—yes, that David, the warrior king—didn’t pretend he was unbreakable.
He wrote what most men are too afraid to admit.
Psalm 38:8 in Hebrew: “נִפְעוֹתִי וְנִדְכֵּאתִי עַד־מְאֹד” (Nif’oti venidkheti ad-me’od) — “I am feeble and crushed beyond measure.”
Crushed.
Not slightly stressed. Not just tired.
Crushed.
And God didn’t reject him for it.
God preserved his words for eternity.
Let that sink in.
The very thing men are taught to hide… God chose to record.
So why are you still pretending?
Why are you still carrying something Jesus already died for?
Because here’s the truth most men don’t want to hear:

Hiding your pain doesn’t make you strong.
It just makes you unavailable—to God, to others, even to yourself.
And the enemy loves a silent man.
Because silence isolates.
And isolation is where lies grow louder than truth.

“Handle it yourself.”
“No one cares anyway.”
“Don’t be weak.”
But Jesus didn’t come for the men who had it all together.
He came for the ones falling apart behind closed doors.

In Matthew 11:28, Jesus says in the original Greek: “Δεῦτε πρός με πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες καὶ πεφορτισμένοι” (Deute pros me pantes hoi kopiontes kai pephortismenoi) — “Come to me, all who are weary and burdened.”
That word “πεφορτισμένοι” (pephortismenoi) means heavily loaded… weighed down… carrying something you were never meant to carry alone.
That’s you, isn’t it?
Still carrying it.
Still smiling through it.
Still telling everyone you’re good when you know you’re not.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
And maybe… just maybe… this is the moment you stop hiding.

Not by posting a perfect life.
Not by pretending you’re healed.
But by surrendering.

Real strength is not silence.
Real strength is surrender.
Because when you finally bring your pain into the light, it loses its power.
When you finally speak what you’ve been suppressing, chains start breaking.
And when you finally let Jesus into the places you’ve locked away…
He doesn’t shame you.
He restores you.
That’s the Gospel.

Not “fix yourself first.”
Not “be strong enough.”
But grace.
Undeserved. Unfiltered. Unstoppable.
The very places you’re ashamed of… are the very places Jesus wants to rewrite.
If something inside you is stirring… don’t ignore it.
Let this become more than a moment—let it become a turning point.
Follow closely if you’re ready for truth that doesn’t just sound good—but actually transforms.
And if you truly want to glorify God—not just in words, but in action—then help this message reach more people who are silently suffering.
Support the mission. Let it breathe beyond you.
Because someone out there is drowning quietly… and this might be the lifeline God uses.
This isn’t just content.
This is calling.
This is discipleship.
This is war against silence.
And if you’re ready to stop hiding and start healing, stay close.
Because the man you’re becoming is waiting on the other side of your surrender.
And Jesus is not afraid of your pain.
He’s waiting in it.
You don’t have to carry it anymore.
